paperInfo.subject: Chemistry
paperInfo.syllabus: A-Level Chemistry Forms 5–6 (ZIMSEC code 6031; current heritage-based syllabus scope)
paperInfo.coverage: Original expanded practice bank synthesised from ZIMSEC syllabus scope and recurring examination-style skills; not a reproduction of copyrighted past-paper text.
paperInfo.source: ZIMSEC official resources (www5.zimsec.co.zw) and syllabus copies hosted on StudyLib (studylib.net).
paperInfo.notes: 150 original MCQs spanning physical, inorganic, organic and analytical chemistry.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes first ionisation energy?

options.text: Energy released when an atom gains an electron
Energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms
Energy required to remove all electrons

questions.explanation: First ionisation energy is the energy required to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms to form gaseous +1 ions.

questions.questionText: Across a period, first ionisation energy generally increases because

options.text: nuclear charge increases while shielding changes little

questions.explanation: Increasing nuclear charge with similar shielding generally strengthens attraction for outer electrons.
